entry.title: Model company for SAP cloud solutions for Architects: From Target Architecture to an Executable Base
entry.content:
Part 2 of a blog series on model company for SAP cloud solutions

Introduction

 

Every architect knows the moment: the target architecture is documented in capability maps, process models and solution designs, but the next question is how to turn that intent into decisions the implementation team can validate and deliver.

This is my second post in the model company for SAP cloud solutions series. The first post introduced the overall proposition and the move toward Fit-to-Standard. Here, the focus is on the decisions enterprise and solution architects need to make.

Model company provides a pre-configured, executable SAP S/4HANA reference baseline with available industry and line-of-business content. It does not define every customer’s target architecture. Instead, it gives architects a working reference against which to assess capability coverage, question assumptions and identify the design decisions that remain.

Figure 1: From architectural intent to an executable reference. Model company provides a baseline for validation, not a finished customer architecture.

The Architect’s Challenge: From Design to Executable Reality

 

Target architectures describe what an organization wants to achieve; implementation teams must determine how that intent can be realized in a configured solution. The handover between the two often exposes uncertainties: Is a process already supported by standard SAP functionality? Which assumptions need testing? What requires integration, configuration or an extension?

Model company helps bridge this gap by making relevant standard processes and industry content tangible. Architects can explore and demonstrate a working reference rather than relying exclusively on diagrams or descriptions. The reference does not remove the need for discovery or customer-specific validation; it makes those activities more focused.

This supports a change in mindset, from Fit-to-Gap (“how do we reproduce what we do today?”) to Fit-to-Standard (“can the standard support the intended outcome, and where is differentiation genuinely necessary?”). The question is not whether the standard is always sufficient, but how to make deviations evidence-based architectural decisions.

Figure 2: Changing the conversation: assess business outcomes against the standard before specifying deviations.

An Architect’s Workflow: A Retail Example

 

Consider an illustrative retail transformation. The target architecture calls for improved inventory visibility, a consistent order-fulfillment process and reliable financial integration. Rather than treating every existing customization as a requirement, the architecture team can use the relevant model company reference to structure its assessment.

  • Identify the capabilities: map the target business outcomes to the processes and application responsibilities that must support them.
  • Explore the baseline: examine available retail processes and associated artifacts in the model company system. Confirm which scope and release are available.
  • Validate assumptions: demonstrate representative flows with sample data; compare the standard with key business scenarios and record the functional or non-functional questions still open.
  • Make design choices: Distinguish standard coverage from required configuration, interfaces, data work, and genuinely differentiating extensions. For each proposed deviation, document its justification, expected business value, and implications for complexity, cost, and long-term maintainability.
  • Carry decisions into delivery: use relevant process models, scope artifacts and governance tools to connect decisions to implementation requirements, testing and change control.

The result is not an automatically generated target architecture. It is a better-evidenced design: the team knows what it has validated, where uncertainty remains and which decisions require architectural ownership.

 

How It Helps Enterprise Architects

 

Enterprise architects connect strategy, business capabilities and the target operating model with the application landscape.

Model company can help them:

  • Assess capability realization in a running reference and distinguish demonstrated scope from capabilities that still require further design.
  • Relate reference business architecture and process models to the actual standard processes delivered in the relevant industry or line of business.
  • Create a shared starting point for business stakeholders, enterprise architecture and delivery teams, reducing misunderstandings about what “standard” means.
  • Inform roadmap and scoping decisions by checking current content availability, release coverage and relevant prerequisites rather than assuming that every planned capability is already delivered.

How It Helps Solution Architects

 

Solution architects translate the target into process, data, application, integration and extension decisions. Against a pre-configured reference, they can:

  • Explore representative end-to-end processes instead of starting each discussion from an unconfigured system.
  • Inspect sample master and transactional data and identify interfaces or integration requirements; a visible integration point does not necessarily mean that a connected external system has been delivered.
  • Evaluate standard functionality first, then select suitable clean-core-aligned extensibility options based on the requirement and deployment environment.
  • Use process and delivery artifacts to support documented scope, requirements and testing decisions, with traceability governed through the chosen project toolchain.

Connecting Architecture to the Delivery Toolchain

 

SAP LeanIX supports enterprise architecture and application landscape decisions; SAP Signavio provides a comprehensive process intelligence and transformation suite for process-modeling and business transformation; and SAP Cloud ALM is a full lifecycle application management platform, covering implementation governance, operations monitoring, and continuous improvement.

For transformation initiatives, it delivers end-to-end project management, structured requirements handling, and test governance, making it the central control point for managing SAP solution deployments.

Model company contributes a working reference and associated artifacts that can be used alongside these tools.

The precise artifacts available depend on the selected model company scope and release. Process models, documentation, test assets and sample data can support design and Fit-to-Standard workshops, but architects should verify what is included and how it can be accessed or imported. Viewing process content and importing or synchronizing it into a customer workspace may have different licensing and authorization requirements.

Importantly, traceability is not automatic. Connecting process models, scope, requirements and test evidence requires tool configuration, appropriate entitlements, disciplined ownership and project governance. SAP Signavio, SAP Cloud ALM synchronization, for example, has defined setup and license prerequisites.

 

Where It Fits in SAP Activate

 

Model company brings its most immediate value to early validation and Fit-to-Standard work, particularly during Explore. Its reference content and artifacts may also inform later implementation phases.

The model company system remains a reference/sandbox environment: it is not the productive customer solution and should not be described as directly deploying into production.

  • Discover and Prepare: use the available baseline to illustrate potential scope, challenge target-state assumptions and prepare more focused architectural discussions.
  • Explore (Fit-to-Standard): run relevant scenarios against the standard, assess business fit, identify genuine deltas and agree which requirements need additional design.
  • Realize: use validated decisions and applicable reference artifacts to guide implementation; govern architecture conformance, interfaces, extensions and test coverage in the customer project.
  • Deploy: confirm that the implemented productive solution meets the approved architecture, security, integration and operational criteria. This is a customer-project responsibility, not a deployment of the model company sandbox.
  • Run: maintain architectural guardrails, assess changing needs against standard capabilities, and govern extensions and process evolution over time.

The continuous thread is controlled decision-making: from intended business capability, through process validation and design, to implementation evidence. The architecture team can establish traceability across that chain but must actively maintain it.

Figure 3: Model company in SAP Activate. Explore is the primary direct validation point; later phases benefit from the reference and decisions carried forward.

Keeping the Core Clean: Extensibility Governance

 

Clean core is an architectural discipline, not a property that eliminates governance. It aims to keep the SAP core close to standard, use appropriate extension mechanisms and released interfaces, and support maintainability and future upgrades. Model company, built on SAP Best Practices that bring standard Line of Business business processes and aligned with clean-core principles, gives architects a useful starting reference, not an unconditional guarantee of customer-specific compliance or upgrade safety.

  • Challenge proposed deviations: demonstrate what standard content already covers before agreeing to custom build; record business rationale and architectural consequences for justified gaps.
  • Choose the right extension pattern: consider approved key-user, developer/on-stack and side-by-side extensibility, including SAP BTP where appropriate. The right choice depends on requirements, release and deployment model; “side-by-side” is not the answer to every extension.
  • Govern integration explicitly: design interfaces around applicable released APIs and supported integration patterns, while validating external systems, security, performance and data responsibilities.
  • Keep decisions traceable: link requirements, architectural decisions, process changes and tests within the project’s governed toolchain, rather than assuming the reference environment does this automatically.

By reducing unnecessary custom code and providing a clean-core-aligned reference, model company simplifies architectural decision-making and lifecycle management, while enabling architects to focus their assessments on customer-specific requirements, integrations, and extensions.

 

What Architects Still Need to Validate

 

A reference baseline is most useful when its boundaries are clear.

Architects must still confirm:

  • Industry and country coverage
  • Business-process fit
  • The customer’s application and integration landscape
  • Data migration and ownership
  • Non-functional requirements
  • Security and regulatory obligations
  • Extension design
  • Licensing or technical prerequisites for connected tools.

The strongest use of model company is therefore not to declare the architecture complete. It is to expose and resolve architectural questions earlier, while keeping legitimate differentiation visible and controlled.

 

From Clean Core to Validated AI Capabilities

 

Clean-core principles, standardized processes, and governed data provide a strong foundation for sustainable AI adoption. Model company for SAP cloud solutions builds on this foundation, with Joule already activated and successfully tested in selected model company environments. In addition, AI use cases have been tested and validated and are ready for inclusion, progressively extending the portfolio’s ability to demonstrate AI-enabled business processes.

For architects, this creates an opportunity to move beyond conceptual AI discussions and explore how intelligent capabilities can be incorporated into business processes and solution architectures. These validated scenarios provide tangible reference points for assessing architectural dependencies, integration requirements, and the potential role of AI within a customer’s target landscape.

AI enablement is progressing across the model company portfolio, with capabilities and availability varying by industry and line of business. Their adoption within a customer environment remains subject to scenario availability, release compatibility, licensing and entitlements, technical prerequisites, and applicable AI consumption arrangements.

By combining a clean-core-aligned baseline with activated Joule capabilities and validated AI use cases, model company helps architects bridge the gap between AI strategy and practical enablement.

 

Conclusion: A Better Starting Point for Architectural Decisions

 

Model company changes the starting point, not the architect’s responsibility. Instead of working only from abstract models or a blank configuration, teams can examine a tangible, SAP-delivered baseline and use it to validate assumptions, challenge unnecessary complexity and make more informed Fit-to-Standard decisions.

Whether your role is enterprise architecture or solution architecture, the benefit is a clearer distinction between what the reference already demonstrates, what the customer genuinely needs and what must still be designed and governed.

Start with one critical capability from your target architecture. Explore the model company content available for the relevant industry, test the associated process assumptions and document where the standard fits or where further decisions are needed.

What is the harder challenge in your projects:

  • Validating standard coverage
  • Designing integrations
  • Governing extensions?

Share your experience in the comments.

For availability and request guidance, consult your model company industry/Line of Business dashboard or contact modelcompany@sap.com. For scope selection and applicable terms, refer to SAP Note 3631601 through your normal SAP support channel.

If you missed Part 1, read Model company for SAP cloud solutions: Your Fast Track to Fit-to-Standard. Upcoming topics will explore the consultant, partner and content/toolchain perspectives.

entry.title: SAP Enterprise Service Management Q3 2026 Innovation Highlights
entry.content:
As SAP's Autonomous Enterprise vision continues to take shape across our portfolio, in Q3 2026 we delivered powerful new capabilities for SAP Enterprise Service Management (SAP ESM) customers, partners, and practitioners. Whether you are modernizing HR service delivery, managing financial shared services, or looking to drive higher self-service adoption across the enterprise and every business function, the Q3 2026 release has something for you.

Before we dive in, we’re excited to share our customers’ value stories! Take a moment to register for our upcoming webinars and hear about our customers’ deployment journeys and value achieved from unified, AI-led, shared service operations with SAP ESM.

🚀Tuesday, November 10, 2026
Cracking the Code on HR Service Delivery: Enercon's Journey
Featuring Enercon's journey in unifying HR shared service delivery, moderated by HR Tech analyst,  Anita Lettink.
Register here.
 
🚀Thursday, November 19, 2026
Smarter, Faster, Unified: SAP’s Journey to AI-Powered Shared Services
SAP’s global deployment with over 4,000 service professionals live today, serving employees, partners, and customers across 7 business functions.
Register here.

Now, let’s dive into the Q3 2026 innovation highlights including insights on autonomous assistants coming your way!  For even more detailed insights on our Q3 2026 service innovations, register here for the Q3 2026 Release Overview on November 5th, hosted by our product management team.

Intelligent case flow: Less effort with faster resolution

Case management in SAP ESM has proven to deliver the flexibility organizations need to model their shared service processes across the enterprise, coordinating complex workflows between automation and human action. The Q3 2026 enhancements to Case Flow reduce manual steps for both service representatives and administrators, allowing structured service processes to progress more naturally and more efficiently without unnecessary intervention.

Auto Complete Conditions for Input Steps in Case Flow

Input steps within a case flow allow service representatives to capture or update structured data in context without navigating away from the case. Until now, however, marking an input step as complete was always a manual action, even when the required conditions were clearly satisfied.

With this Q3 2026 release, administrators can now define conditions under which an input step will automatically mark itself as complete. When those conditions are met, for example, when specific field values have been set or when a case reaches a particular status, the system evaluates the configured logic and completes the step without requiring a service representative to take action.

Why it matters:

  • High-volume, structured processes benefit most. Think onboarding workflows, procurement inquiries, or HR case handling where multiple input steps follow predictable completion patterns.
  • Service representatives can focus on the steps that genuinely require their judgment, rather than clicking through steps the system can already identify as complete.
  • Administrators retain full control over when auto-completion applies, using the same familiar condition builder available throughout the Case Designer.

Auto Trigger for Case Approval Step

Approval steps in SAP ESM case flows are a critical governance mechanism, ensuring that key decisions are reviewed by the right people before a case proceeds. However, a common source of delay in approval-heavy workflows is simply that service representatives forget, or are too busy, to manually submit the approval request.

This enhancement allows administrators to configure an approval step to auto-submit as soon as its preconditions are met. Once the case reaches the configured state and all entry conditions are satisfied, the approval request is triggered automatically, without service representative intervention.

Why it matters:

  • Eliminates a common bottleneck in approval-gated workflows, particularly in financial shared services and compliance-driven processes where timely approvals are essential.
  • Works alongside existing precondition configuration, giving administrators precise control over when auto-submission is appropriate.
  • Approvers still receive requests and must act. This feature automates the submission, not the decision itself.

Accelerate Financial Service Delivery with Contract Accounts

For organizations delivering financial shared services, whether handling billing inquiries, payment disputes, collection workloads, or contract account management, having complete financial context within the service case is not a nice-to-have; it is essential. The Q3 2026 release introduces a deeply integrated Contract Account View, connecting SAP ESM directly to SAP Cloud ERP FI-CA financial data and bringing it into the agent's hands without the need to switch systems.

Contract Account View: Financial Documents, Invoices, Payments, and Collections

Service representatives working on financial inquiries can now see a complete picture of the customer's financial position right from the ESM agent desktop, without navigating to SAP Cloud ERP transaction screens. These include:

  • Financial Documents and Open Items: All FI-CA transactions for the past 365 days (configurable) are displayed, aggregated by document number.
  • Invoices: The last 12 months of invoices, billing documents, and billing plans are available, each with a direct link to the PDF printout.
  • Payments: All payment documents posted in the last 365 days are visible with real-time, color-coded status tags.
  • Collections: The full collections history from SAP Cloud ERP FI-CA is surfaced directly in ESM, covering dunning records, returns, and write-offs.

Contract Account View: Payment Arrangements, Locks, and Correspondence

Beyond raw financial data, the Contract Account View also provides service representatives with the context needed to understand active agreements, account restrictions, and prior correspondence, all without leaving the service agent desktop.

  • Payment Arrangements: All Promise to Pay agreements and Installment Plans for the contract account are visible in either card or table format.
  • Locks: Active and expired locks applied to the contract account are displayed, including lock type, reason, and date range.
  • Correspondences and Bank Data: Complete correspondence history, key attributes, and bank data, are available in a dedicated tab.

This provides service representatives with a comprehensive financial picture in one place.

Elevating the self-service experience

The self-service application is how employees experience enterprise service management directly. Two Q3 2026 enhancements give administrators more precise control over what employees see and how they interact with their cases, resulting in a cleaner, more focused experience and fewer unnecessary support contacts.

Controlled Case Visibility in List View

In organizations where SAP ESM supports multiple lines of business, not every case type is intended for employee self-service visibility. With this Q3 2026 update, a new attribute has been added to the case type configuration to specify self-service relevance. Only cases belonging to case types that have been marked as self-service relevant in Case Type Configuration will appear in the employee's list. Cases associated with internal, service representative-only, or back-office case types will not be visible in the self-service interface.

Why it matters:

  • Employees see only the cases that are relevant and actionable for them, reducing confusion and erroneous selection.
  • Administrators gain precise control over the self-service experience, aligning what employees see with the organization's service delivery model.
  • This is particularly valuable for organizations running ESM across multiple functions such as HR, Finance, IT, and Procurement, where different case types serve very different audiences.

Enhanced Case Communication History

Understanding the full history of a case, including who said what, when, and through which channel, is fundamental to the self-service experience. Before this release, timeline events and case conversations were combined in a single Conversations tab, which made it harder to quickly locate a particular event or communication.

This enhancement restructures how case history is presented in the self-service interface, making it easier to locate specific events and communications, reducing inquiries back to the service representative and improving resolution times.

Why it matters:

  • A dedicated Timeline tab now presents all case events in chronological order, including status changes, assignments, workflow transitions, and other system-level activities, giving employees a clear audit trail of everything that has happened on their case.
  • The Conversations tab has been refined to focus on actual communications. A new Past Conversations section surfaces all non-internal notes, providing employees with a clear record of the dialogue between them and the service team.
  • Internal notes intended only for service representatives remain hidden from the employee-facing view, ensuring operational transparency is maintained without exposing confidential service team communications.

Preview: Autonomous Assistants

One of the most exciting themes at SAP SAPPHIRE and SAP Connect was the emergence of autonomous, AI-led assistants within SAP ESM. These are not incremental improvements to existing features; they represent a fundamentally different way of working, where Joule Work takes on complex, multi-step service and finance tasks with contextual intelligence and minimal human intervention. We are pleased to share an early look at two assistants currently progressing through Early Adopter Care, with general availability coming soon.

Recurring Receivables Assistant

Managing recurring revenue operations at scale is complex. Collections specialists, invoicing teams, subscription managers, and accounts receivable clerks each work within their own slice of a highly interconnected process, and when an exception occurs, resolving it typically requires manual coordination across multiple systems and stakeholders.

The Recurring Receivables Assistant coordinates execution across subscription orders and contracts, invoices, disputes, payments, and collections. The assistant helps teams prioritize collections, manage subscription contract changes, correct invoices, and resolve customer disputes and payment exceptions across multiple applications and solutions with clearer issue context and faster customer communication.

The assistant supports the core business stages across the receivables lifecycle:

  • Prioritize: Surfaces high-impact accounts, explains risk drivers, and recommends the next-best collection action, so collections specialists focus effort where it matters most.
  • Prevent: Detects invoice rejection risk before downstream impact occurs, identifies likely root causes, and recommends corrections, reducing exceptions before they slow collections.
  • Correct: Identifies contract data issues, validates corrections, simulates billing impact, and guides subscription specialists through the update, unblocking invoice and payment flow.
  • Resolve: Investigates payment exceptions and unmatched payments, connects invoice and contract context, and guides AR clerks through resolution, closing issues with less manual investigation.

Case Management Assistant

Every service representative manages cases, but the experience of working through a complex, multi-step case, coordinating with customers, extracting information from attachments, triggering backend processes, and knowing what to do next, can still be demanding and time-consuming. The Case Management Assistant is designed to change that.

Available as a standalone starting point for a service interaction or embedded directly in the SAP ESM agent desktop, the Case Management Assistant is a Joule-powered AI agent that works alongside service representatives throughout the full case lifecycle. 

Key dimensions of the assistant's capability include:

  • Contextual guidance: The assistant understands where a case is in its workflow and surfaces relevant next steps, so service representatives spend less time figuring out what to do and more time doing it.
  • Document and entity extraction: Attachments, emails, and case descriptions are automatically analyzed to extract key information, reducing manual data entry and improving case accuracy from the outset.
  • Communication assistance: Service representatives receive assistance drafting and refining customer communications within the case, ensuring timely and consistent responses that reflect the service organization's standards.
  • Connected process execution: The assistant can trigger actions in connected SAP systems, such as SAP Cloud ERP, directly from the case context, without requiring service representatives to navigate to separate applications.

Early adopter customers are actively engaged, already reporting measurable reductions in service representative effort. Stay tuned for the general availability announcement, coming soon.

Additional Information

For additional Q3 2026 innovations relevant for SAP Enterprise Service Management, register for the upcoming Q3 2026 Release Webinar. To stay up-to-date as we release capabilities each month and to get a full view of what’s new for Q3 2026, reference the What’s New page in our help portal. entry.title: What If Joule Could Help You Complete the Business-Driven Configuration Questionnaire? Now It Can.
entry.content:
A successful SAP S/4HANA Cloud implementation starts with understanding how a business works—and translating that understanding into the right configuration. The Business-Driven Configuration Questionnaire (BDCQ), a structured accelerator within the SAP Activate methodology, helps make that connection. Line of Business (LoB) configuration experts use it to gather the configuration values that will ultimately be entered in SAP Central Business Configuration for the customer’s SAP S/4HANA Cloud development system tenants.

More than a questionnaire, the BDCQ is a bridge between SAP consultants and customer business users. It helps ensure that solution configuration reflects real business requirements, both before and during Fit-to-Standard workshops.

Why does the BDCQ matter?

  • It provides early insight into the customer’s business processes and configuration needs.
  • It offers prescriptive guidance on identifying configuration requirements aligned with the implementation scope.
  • It provides a secondary validation of whether SAP S/4HANA Cloud Public Edition (Public Cloud) is the right fit for the customer, complementing the Digital Discovery Assessment (DDA).
  • It brings greater structure to the planning and delivery of Fit-to-Standard Analysis workshops.
  • It supports productive conversations between implementation experts and business users during workshops.
  • It connects customer business processes directly to solution configuration activities, including references to specific SSCUI apps or SSCUI groups.

The BDCQ captures two levels of information at different stages of the project:

The value of the BDCQ goes beyond collecting configuration data. It also helps LoB configuration experts build relationships with customer LoB experts and introduces those experts to SAP S/4HANA Cloud early in the project. Ideally, the same customer experts who provide L2 responses will take part in Fit-to-Standard workshops and user acceptance testing before go-live. In this way, the BDCQ also supports the project’s broader change-management effort.

Not every BDCQ maps neatly to a traditional line of business. The implementation team should therefore confirm that all business processes selected in the Digital Discovery Assessment are covered across the available BDCQs. Any remaining processes—for example, Human Resources or Two-Tier ERP—should be assigned based on transferable expertise and team availability.

So, how can AI-assisted support make it easier to complete the BDCQ?

During the Prepare phase, open Perform Initial Business Process Assessment for SAP S/4HANA Cloud. You’ll find the ✦ AI-Assisted Procedure session there.

Open the session and follow the instructions for working with the BDCQ Experts.

For example, the BDCQ-FI Expert can guide you through the questionnaire in a conversational manner. Start the conversation, answer its questions, and review the highlights and key points that deserve attention. This provides structured support as you work through the information required for your BDCQ.

The result is a BDCQ populated with Critical Steps, Scope Items, open items, and potential blockers—as illustrated in the example below.

entry.title: Track Your Private Cloud Journey: New Adoption Milestones powered by SAP EarlyWatch Alert
entry.content:
We are excited to announce a new capability for SAP S/4HANA Cloud Private Edition customers: adoption milestone tracking, powered by SAP EarlyWatch Alert data and available in the Customer Insights Dashboard (CID) on SAP for Me.

If you are already familiar with the onboarding milestones for SAP S/4HANA Cloud Public Edition and SAP Integrated Business Planning (IBP), this is the Private Cloud counterpart you have been waiting for. And it goes even further: in addition to tracking implementation progress, the new milestones include built-in adoption risk monitoring that continuously watches for early signs of stalled implementations or declining system usage.

 

Why This Matters

Moving to SAP S/4HANA Cloud Private Edition is one of the most significant transformations a business can undertake. The journey from contract signature to a fully operational, value-generating system can span months, sometimes even years, of provisioning, configuration, testing and go-live activities.

Yet for much of that journey, the signals that indicate whether a customer is progressing as expected, or beginning to stall, have been difficult to surface systematically. Data was fragmented across tools, inputs were manual, and adoption risk was often identified too late for meaningful intervention.

The question we set out to answer: How can we generate data-driven insights on adoption journeys, early enough to make a real difference?

 

What SAP EarlyWatch Alert Brings to the Table

SAP EarlyWatch Alert has been a trusted companion for SAP customers for decades, indicating system health, performance, and configuration. With this new release, SAP EarlyWatch Alert further expands its scope beyond system diagnostics into adoption intelligence. Here is what makes this approach unique:

  • Zero configuration. SAP EarlyWatch Alert already collects weekly telemetry data from every connected system: active users, transport activity, transaction usage, and more. No additional setup is required from the customer.
  • Fully automated. Milestones are automatically recalculated twice per week across all connected S/4HANA Private Cloud landscapes.
  • Proactive risk detection. The dashboard does not just track forward progress. It also continuously monitors signs of stalled adoption and user decline after go-live.
  • Integrated experience. Milestone data appears in the Onboarding tab of the Customer Insights Dashboard in SAP for Me, right alongside Public Cloud and IBP milestones.

The SAP EarlyWatch Alert Apps as tools for proactive alerting and diagnostics can be accessed via SAP for Me: https://me.sap.com/servicessupport/diagnostics

 

The Six Adoption Milestones

Each SAP S/4HANA Cloud Private Edition system landscape is tracked through six milestones that map to the key phases of a new cloud ERP implementation or transformation approach. Milestones are evaluated per system track, which is the logical grouping of a customer's Development (DEV), Test (TEST), and Production (PROD) systems linked by a common SAP Transport Management System route.

M1: Landscape Initialized

Your S/4HANA Cloud Private Edition system is live and connected to SAP. Your implementation journey has now begun.

This milestone is triggered when the first EarlyWatch Alert data is received from any non-production system in the track. It marks the moment the landscape becomes visible to SAP. No thresholds and no configuration are needed. The mere presence of this data confirms that provisioning is complete and the system is connected.

M2: Realize Phase Active

Your team has started configuring the system for your business needs. Build and testing activities are now underway.

Detected through usage of transaction SPRO (the SAP Customizing Implementation Guide) on a DEV or TEST system. SPRO is the central entry point for system configuration, so its usage is a reliable signal that the implementation team has begun tailoring the system to the customer's business processes.

M3: Pre-Cutover Preparation

Access roles and authorization profiles are being set up. Go-live preparation is underway.

Detected through usage of transaction PFCG (Role Maintenance) on a non-production system. Setting up authorization roles and user profiles is a critical pre-go-live activity.

M4: Cutover Initiated

Your team has initiated the cutover; configuration is being transported to your production system. Go-live is imminent.

Triggered when a significant transport wave is detected on the production system: at least 1,000 Workbench and Customizing transport objects imported in a single week. This threshold distinguishes genuine cutover deployments from routine maintenance imports and provides a high-confidence signal that go-live preparation is in its final stage.

M5: Go-Live Detected

A significant jump in active users on your production system confirms go-live. Your system is now in productive use.

SAP EarlyWatch Alert tracks weekly active user counts on the production system. When a significant and sustained spike in users is detected, the system is considered live. The detection automatically adapts to the size of each customer's landscape, so it works equally well for small and large deployments. It also accounts for special cases like system conversions and filters out technical-only activity to avoid false positives.

M6: Steady Usage State

Your system is in stable productive use with an active user base and regular updates. The status is reviewed continuously and may change.

Unlike M1 through M5, which are set once and remain, M6 is a living indicator. It is re-evaluated every week and can change between "Reached" (healthy) and "At Risk" based on two independent checks.

M6-1: Transport Activity Check. Were any transports imported into any system in the track within the last six months? If not, the system may no longer be actively maintained. This check runs independently of go-live status, so it can flag adoption stalls even before a customer has gone live.

M6-2: User Decline Detection. After go-live, the system continuously monitors whether the number of active users on the production system is declining significantly. A sustained drop in usage serves as an early signal for customer success teams to reach out and offer support.

Remark: Some milestones can be calculated based on the availability of connected Private Cloud systems.

 

Where to Find It

The milestone data is available in the Customer Insights Dashboard (CID) on SAP for Me, in the Onboarding tab: https://me.sap.com/reporting/customerinsightsdashboard/onboarding

If you are already using the Onboarding view for SAP S/4HANA Cloud Public Edition or SAP IBP, you will find the Private Cloud milestones right alongside them. Same dashboard, same experience, no additional setup:

When M6 turns red, it provides a specific, actionable signal: either maintenance activity has stopped or the productive user base is declining. Both are leading indicators of adoption challenges, and both are surfaced early enough for proactive engagement.

 

Conclusion

Adoption milestone tracking for SAP S/4HANA Cloud Private Edition transforms EarlyWatch Alert data, collected every week from every connected system, into structured, actionable adoption intelligence. By automatically identifying where each customer stands in their cloud journey and flagging early signs of risk, it enables the kind of proactive, data-driven engagement that complex cloud transformations demand.

Read more about how this helps you get the most out of your SAP investment: Proactive by Design: Introducing Adoption Milestone Tracking for S/4HANA Private Cloud - SAP Community

The data is already there. Now, it tells a story.

entry.title: Changelog for SAP objects - Verify clean core level C compliance of your custom extensions
entry.content:
In the clean core level concept outlined in the Clean core extensibility for SAP S/4HANA Cloud whitepaper, custom extensions using arbitrary SAP internal objects can be qualified as conditional clean core Level C extensions if dedicated pre‑upgrade checks based on changelog for SAP objects are executed for these extensions.

 Internal SAP objects can change at any point in time during an upgrade. Incompatible changes include, for example, deletion of objects, renaming or deletion of parameters or methods and others.

 To detect in custom code the usage of SAP internal objects, which have been incompatibly changed, SAP now provides the changelog for SAP objects, which contains the names of all SAP standard objects (and their associated components like methods or parameters), that have undergone incompatible changes in the new release. Technically, the changelog information is transferred via the Simplification Database infrastructure from the SAP Support Portal to your system. You can download it from the SAP Software Download Center of the SAP Support Portal and import it into your ABAP test cockpit (ATC) check system.

The changelog information is integrated and considered in the clean core ATC check Usage of APIs which can then detect in custom code the use of SAP objects and their associated components (sub-objects), that have been incompatibly changed.  

 SAP recommendation is to consider changelog during regular ATC quality checks to identify, early in the development process, any usages in custom code of SAP internal objects that have undergone incompatible changes. The changelog information should be included in the ATC check at the latest before the system upgrade, following the same approach as for the ATC checks related to the SAP S/4HANA simplification items.

 This will help to better estimate the risk of custom code not functioning properly after the next release upgrade.

Current functional scope

 The changelog provides information of incompatible changes affecting SAP APIs classified as released API, classic API, or internal API.

It focuses on the deletion of SAP development objects and their associated components (sub-objects) for the following object types:

  • Classes
  • Interfaces
  • Function modules
  • CDS views (DDLS)

 Deletions are reported as warnings for both the affected objects and their sub-objects. These include methods, attributes, types, method and function module parameters, and CDS view fields.

 The current changelog version covers deletions introduced during upgrades from SAP S/4HANA 2023 to SAP S/4HANA 2025, helping developers identify potentially incompatible changes in SAP development objects and assess their impact on custom code.

Prerequisites

In your SAP S/4HANA 2023 or later system (private cloud or on-premise)  you are adopting the clean core level concept outlined in the Clean core extensibility for SAP S/4HANA Cloud whitepaper and following the ABAP test cockpit (ATC) recommendations for governance of clean core ABAP development. You have already configured the Usage of APIs clean core check in your ATC system.

Setup

First download the changelog with the Simplification Database (SAP Note 3693326 (part 1)). As a result, the changelog.zip file is downloaded to your drive.

Next to enable the changelog functionality implement the relevant SAP Note 3758771 - Changelog Support in Usage of API ATC check.

Once the SAP Note has been implemented, upload the changelog content to the system in which the ATC check runs.

  • Remote ATC setup: Upload the changelog content to the central ATC check system.
  • Local ATC setup: Upload the changelog content to the local ATC system.

 PLEASE NOTE: If you are already using ATC on SAP BTP as your central ATC check system for your systems landscape, you can upload and use the changelog in your local SAP S/4HANA 2023 system, as the changelog functionality is not yet available in ATC on SAP BTP.

 To upload the changelog content on your ATC system go to the ABAP Editor (SE38) and execute the SYCM_API_CLASSIFICATION_MANAGR program (F8):

Click on the button Upload API File (Ctrl + F3), choose "Changelog" as a file type in the popup dialog and click on the Confirm. Select the previously downloaded changelog.zip file from your drive.

Once you see the uploaded file with data type "Changelog" in the Data Sources overview, the changelog is active and will report findings when running the ATC check "Usage of APIs".

NOTE: Only one file of the data type "Changelog" can exist in the Data Sources overview. To update the changelog, first delete the existing file, then upload a new version by following the steps described above.

How to use changelog in a pre-upgrade scenario

Execute an ATC run using any check variant containing the Usage Of APIs ATC check over your custom code in the system. In the list of ATC findings, you will see the issues related to the changelog, clearly recognizable from the Check Message text:

In the details of a changelog related ATC finding, you will see more information regarding your incompatibility issue reported by the changelog:

How to use changelog during development

It is recommended to consider changelog also during your development process. For this purpose your ATC check variant, used during development process, must contain the Usage of APIs check along with the changelog information.

In this example ABAP_CLOUD_DEVELOPMENT check variant is used in the development system, and the Usage of APIs check considers the changelog information. The changelog related ATC findings will be displayed with detailed check messages in the ATC result:

What’s next

Support for the changelog in ATC on SAP BTP is already on the short-term roadmap. The changelog approach for SAP S/4HANA 2025 FPS levels and future SAP S/4HANA versions will be communicated soon.

entry.title: Joule Agents on SAP Cloud ERP Private: What Really Happens When You Try to Activate One
entry.content:
There are three ways to get a Joule agent working on SAP Cloud ERP Private. Before any of them matters, there is one check that decides whether a single one of them is open to you.

You have AI Units on the contract. Business Data Cloud is provisioned. Finance has an approved use case and a sponsor.

Someone asks you the obvious question: "We have S/4HANA, Business Data Cloud and AI Units. So which agents do we build in S/4, and which ones on BDC?"

It is a good question from a well prepared team, and it contains a category error. Neither S/4HANA nor Business Data Cloud is a place where agents are built. But that is not the reason the project stalls. You open the agent's Discovery Center page, and the minimum release is SAP S/4HANA 2025 FPS01, restricted to Early Adopter Care. Production is on 2023. Today the answer is not one platform or the other. It is none of the three paths, and nobody in the conversation had mentioned it.

There is also something that has to be settled before any of that, and it is not one of the three paths.

It is the release. On SAP Cloud ERP Private the minimum release differs per agent. The Accounting Accruals Agent used in this example requires S/4HANA 2025 FPS01, and at the time of writing it is available only to customers enrolled in Early Adopter Care. Check each agent against SAP Note 3789370 rather than assuming a common floor.

Once a landscape is above that line, two things decide which path applies: what the thing has to produce when it finishes, and how far it has to reach to produce it. Answer those and the path picks itself.

So this post does two things. It establishes where to check that first, and then it walks the three paths that the choice is actually between, with one finance process carried along each of them.

Reach drawn as radius. Each path stops at a boundary, and that boundary is the reason the next one exists.

Three words worth getting right

Most of the confusion in these conversations is vocabulary, not architecture.

Term

What it actually is

Joule Assistant

The orchestrator. It takes the user's intent, plans the work, picks which agents to invoke, sequences them, and assembles the answer. It decides the what and the when.

Joule Agent

A task executor with a narrow, pre-defined scope. It decides how to accomplish its objective inside that scope. It does not control the wider flow.

Agent Extension

A Joule Studio solution type. SAP's own description: custom skills, instructions or data fields added to existing SAP agents.

The last one is the one most people have never heard of, and it is the one that resolves the majority of these conversations.

And a second set, because SAP renamed the products

In 2025 SAP renamed its cloud ERP offerings, and the rename is still visible in some places and not others. The old and new names both circulate.

  • SAP Cloud ERP was S/4HANA Cloud, public edition. Multi-tenant, SAP schedules the upgrades, no deferral, standard code cannot be modified. The journey is SAP GROW.
  • SAP Cloud ERP Private was S/4HANA Cloud, private edition. Single tenant, the customer schedules upgrades and can defer them, full ABAP development. The journey is RISE with SAP.
  • SAP HANA Cloud is not ERP at all. It is a managed database service on BTP, and it is what Datasphere and Business Data Cloud sit on. Every S/4HANA system uses a HANA database internally, but that is not the product. A customer who says "we are on HANA Cloud" has told you about their data platform and nothing about their ERP.

That confusion matters more than it looks. Before you can compare paths you need to know which ERP edition the customer runs, because the edition decides which agents exist for them at all. The same agent can be available on one edition and absent on the other, so an answer about their data platform does not answer the question you asked.

Path one: activate what SAP already delivers

The test for this path is simple. Does SAP's encoded logic already match how the customer works? If it does, nothing gets built.

Take the SAP Accounting Accruals Agent, reached through the Financial Closing Assistant, as the worked example. Here is what actually happens.

An accountant asks in Joule to prepare accruals for a period and company code. The Assistant routes the intent to the agent. The agent reads two things: the company's own accrual policy handbook, uploaded as a document, and transaction data in the Universal Journal, which includes open purchase orders, goods receipts without an invoice, prepayments and the GR/IR clearing account, plus what is already posted for the period so it does not duplicate. It applies the policy rules against a configured materiality threshold, and produces journal entry proposals, each one carrying a plain-language rationale naming the transactions and the rule it applied.

Those proposals land in the Manage Accrual Proposals Fiori app, where a GL accountant accepts, modifies or rejects each one and posts the accepted entries.

The agent does not post. That is the product, not a configuration choice. That single fact answers most of what a finance team wants to know before it lets an agent near the ledger.

Two things about this flow that surprise people

First, a delivered agent is reading the organisation's own document. If you assume that an SAP-delivered agent cannot read your own documents, you will start building a custom agent when uploading a file would have been enough. That single assumption is the most common reason teams reach for Build when Activate would have worked.

The handbook has real constraints worth knowing before you promise anything. It is uploaded by asking Joule for it from the Manage Accrual Proposals app. It must be a PDF, it supports a maximum of five expense categories before proposal generation times out, and it must name company codes, expense categories and calculation rules, with everything for a given company code in one document. A new upload overwrites the previous one immediately, with no versioning and no approval workflow, which is worth knowing before a period close depends on it.

Second, the minimum release is per agent, not per product. On SAP Cloud ERP Private the Autonomous Finance agents currently require S/4HANA 2025 FPS01. The SAP Discovery Center pages for the Accounting Accruals Agent and the Receivables and Payables Clearing Agent both state that version, and both list the agent as available only to customers enrolled in an Early Adopter Care programme. SAP Note 3789370 carries the same picture for Private Edition. Check the agent's own page against the system's release rather than relying on a product-level answer.

Activation is not a project. It is three things: switching the agent on, writing the policy document it reads, and training the people who work the review app. You know it worked when the team closes one period with the agent running beside them. If that is all the customer needs, stop here. There is no reason to look at the other two paths.

Path two: extend what SAP delivers

The test here is the one that separates most real conversations from imagined ones. Is this the same output, computed by a different rule?

If the customer's process produces the same thing SAP's agent produces but arrives at it differently, you extend. You do not replace.

Agent Extensions are a named solution type in Joule Studio, alongside Agents, n8n Workflows and Applications. SAP's Architecture Center describes what one consists of in a single line: custom skills, instructions or data fields added to existing SAP agents. Three things, named.

Stay with the accruals example. Suppose the business accrues freight from contracted lane rates held in a custom field on the purchase order, while SAP's logic reads invoice history. And suppose the European company codes work to a different materiality threshold from the US ones. Neither of those is a new process. Both still end in an accrual proposal, reviewed in the
same app and posted to the same ledger. That is the test for Extend rather than Build: the thing the agent produces does not change, only the rule that produces it. Three changes cover it. A custom data field makes the lane rate visible to the calculation.
A custom instruction sets materiality by company code instead of one global number. And a custom skill calls a control the delivered agent does not know about.

What the customer keeps

This is the part most often left out of the comparison.

  • SAP's data reads stay as delivered
  • The output is still an accrual proposal, carrying its reasoning
  • SAP keeps maintaining and upgrading the delivered agent, so the underlying logic stays their responsibility rather than becoming yours. With a custom agent, that maintenance moves to you.
  • SAP keeps maintaining and upgrading the delivered agent, so the underlying logic stays their responsibility rather than becoming yours. With a custom agent, that maintenance moves to you.

That last point matters more than it looks. Extend, and the agent is positioned to inherit SAP's next version. Rebuild the same thing from scratch and it has to be maintained against every release, which is a cost that shows up in year two rather than year one.

Two honest limits

Extensions do not port between editions. SAP's clean core guidance puts it plainly: extensions created for private edition generally require adaptations to be portable to the public cloud, side-by-side extensions on BTP are more likely to be compatible because they decouple the logic from the core, and complete parity is not guaranteed because API availability and scope differ across editions. There is a second, more practical point at the time of writing. Every published extension tutorial targets a Public Edition agent, and I could not find one that extends a Private Edition agent. Whether that reflects what the catalogue actually offers, or only what has been written up so far, I cannot tell from public sources. Worth checking against your own tenant rather than taking from a post.

And the upgrade behaviour is positioning, not a published guarantee. SAP has built extension as the path that respects the release train, and that is the architectural intent. The mechanism itself is not documented, and extension points appear to be declared per agent rather than universally. Worth confirming for the specific agent rather than assuming it holds generally.

Path three: build in Joule Studio

The test for this one: is the output a different thing entirely?

If what the customer wants does not exist as an SAP business object, no delivered agent will ever produce it, because it is not an SAP process. It is this company's question. That is when you build, and it is the only honest reason to.

Stay with finance and the shape is obvious. The accruals agent produces a proposal. Suppose the CFO wants something else: two weeks before close, what the accrual exposure is likely to land at across the whole group, including commitments sitting in a third-party receivables platform that never enters S/4HANA, compared against the same quarter in prior years that the ERP no longer keeps online.

That is not an accrual proposal. It is a briefing with a recommendation. Different object, so neither activate nor extend can reach it.

What a Joule Studio agent is actually made of

An agent is a definition plus a set of tools, not a programme.

The definition carries a name, a description, its expertise and its instructions, and Joule uses that description to decide when to route a request to it. You select a model available through the generative AI hub. Then you add tools. The assignable tool types today are:

  • Joule Skills, single deterministic actions
  • Actions, API calls to SAP or third-party systems
  • Automations, Build Process Automation workflows
  • Document grounding resource groups
  • MCP server tools, reached over BTP destinations
  • Other custom agents, used as subagents
  • Human-in-the-loop confirmation points, so the agent pauses for approval at the decisions that matter

This is where Business Data Cloud genuinely belongs, and notice that it arrived on the third path rather than the first. A question that spans entities, spans years and spans systems is exactly what the data layer exists for, and almost nothing before this point needed it.

One limit people assume away

A custom agent can use other custom agents as subagents. It cannot call an SAP-delivered agent. The current interoperability model works inbound: a third-party or custom agent can invoke a delivered Joule Agent through the Agent Gateway. The reverse, a Joule Studio agent calling a delivered SAP agent, is a later iteration, and Joule orchestrating mixed chains of delivered and custom agents is planned rather than shipped.

So a design that assumes a new agent will delegate to the Accruals Agent needs checking before it reaches a whiteboard.

One more thing worth stating plainly, because it is the first question anyone responsible for the ledger will ask: a custom agent runs in the calling user's security context. SAP's own product page puts it directly, saying that all agent traffic flows through the agent gateway, so agents can only execute what the end user has permission to do directly. An agent is not a route around access control.

 

One front door, three places the work lands, and only the third reaching outside the ERP.

The boundary nobody checks

Everything above is about choosing a path. This section is about whether the customer's use case is reachable from any of them, and it is the part most often skipped.

An agent activation is scoped to one backend and one client.

The mechanism is the skills mapping. Each agent has pre-defined Joule Skills that map to specific intended back ends, and only back ends with official, delivered skills are eligible targets for that agent's execution. Routing follows the step ownership defined in the delivered process. There is no mechanism for a single active agent to query or route across multiple clients or backend systems within one conversation turn.

Joule can surface agents from different connected systems in the same interface, which is why this is easy to miss. But each agent still executes against the backend its skills were mapped to, and SAP's product page states the permission boundary directly: all agent traffic flows through the agent gateway, so agents can only execute what the end user has permission to do directly.

How many systems one Joule instance can front is a separate question, and SAP's documentation currently disagrees with itself about it. The constraints pages say a Joule instance links to a single S/4HANA system. The Q2 2026 release notes and the Joule Feature Summary Document say Joule supports connecting multiple Private Edition and Public Edition systems within one formation. Until those reconcile it is not a number worth quoting. What holds either way is the agent-level constraint above: whatever Joule can front, an individual agent still executes against one backend.

Why this decides so many conversations

Consider a landscape with one production client live today and further regional clients built and tested but not yet promoted. Everything works. The agent sits in the live client, reads what it needs, proposes, a person posts.

Now the regional waves land. Each client that goes live needs its own activation, and each of those agents executes against its own client. Joule can front all of them, so a user still asks one question and is routed to the right system. What no single agent does is reason across all five in one turn.

One activation per client. Joule fronts all of them; no single agent reasons across them.

So the question that genuinely spans the clients is not answered by any delivered agent, and it is not answered by an extension either, because extending changes the rule and not the reach. It is answerable where those clients converge, which is the data layer. That is the honest case for Business Data Cloud, and it is a better case than the one usually made for it, because it comes from a constraint rather than from a product sheet.

This belongs alongside the release check, before the catalogue is opened at all. A use case whose data sits in another client, another instance, or in a legacy ERP that only replicates financial documents in, is not reachable from the activate path however many AI Units are already paid for.

What this looks like in a real landscape

A worked example makes this concrete. What follows is a real customer environment with the identifying detail stripped out. Nothing in it is unusual, and that is exactly why it is worth walking through.

They run Cloud ERP Private on release 2023, with a second landscape on release 2025 being built in parallel. Production carries one business client. Several further clients exist in quality and development, configured and tested, waiting on the regional rollout. Central Finance is live, replicating financial documents in from legacy ERP systems still running finance in some parts of the world.

Four things follow from that. The first three are checkable; the fourth is a question I could not resolve.

None of the three paths is open to them yet. The finance agents need 2025 FPS01 and Early Adopter Care enrolment, and the business runs on 2023. The second landscape is where the paths become available, so the first move is finishing that migration, not choosing between agents.

This limit is not theoretical, and it already has a date. With one production client today, one activation covers the whole business and nobody runs into a boundary. When the regional clients go live, each one needs its own agent, and no single agent can answer a question that spans them. That is the moment Build becomes the honest answer, and the go-live date for those clients is already in somebody's plan.

Central Finance changes what the agent can see. The accruals agent reads open purchase orders, goods receipts without an invoice, and the GR/IR clearing account. Central Finance replicates financial and controlling postings plus a defined subset of logistics through the accounting view of logistics. That is an accounting view, not the logistics document chain. Whether it satisfies what the agent's logic expects is a real question, and I have not seen it answered publicly. The practical consequence is that processes posted natively in the live client are reachable, and regions still running in a legacy ERP are not.

Almost the whole surrounding stack is already there. Cloud Identity Services, Build Work Zone, the connectivity and destination services, Integration Suite and the Business AI Platform are all live in the production landscape, as are Business Data Cloud and Datasphere. When the release does arrive, this is a configuration exercise rather than a procurement one, which is worth establishing on any landscape early.

Four questions, in order

These work on any process, not only finance, and they take about five minutes.

Which release is it on, and is the agent available there?

The product, the release and the feature pack, then that agent's own Discovery Center page. On Cloud ERP Private the finance agents need 2025 FPS01 and Early Adopter Care enrolment. Below that line there is no path to choose yet, and every question after this one is academic.

What does it produce, and where is the data?

A posted document, a cleared item, a proposal for review, or a briefing. If the output is the same business object SAP's agent already produces, the answer is path one or two. A different object means path three. Then: which client holds the data it needs, because one agent reads one backend and one client.

Is the gap the process, or the rule?

Does SAP's agent do the right job the wrong way, or the wrong job entirely? Right job, wrong way is an extension, and it is usually a few fields and an instruction. Wrong job entirely is the only honest reason to build. This is the question most often skipped, and skipping it is how a few fields and an instruction turn into a project.

Does the non-SAP system supply data, or make decisions?

A non-SAP system is either a source you read from or a system that acts on its own. Reading its data is a connection you configure, which keeps you on the Build path with a shape you can scope and price. Having that system make decisions on your behalf is a different problem, and not all of it is available today. Answering this question tells you whether Build means a data connection you can commit to now, or something you should not promise yet.

Most of these conversations start at Build, because that is the conversation the market has trained everyone to have. Starting at the release and working down is the shorter route to something that actually ships.

ここでのアップデートとは、SAP HANA2.0内でのリリースへの更新(マイナーまたはインクリメンタルリリースへの更新)をリクエストすることを示しています。

SAP HANAアップデートに利用するSRテンプレートは下記となります。

SAP HANAバージョンアップデート

SRを上げる際に、SAP HANAのSIDを選択してから、各パラメータを指定していただけますようお願いします。

パラメータTarget DB Version

2235581 - SAP HANA: Supported Operating Systems 

なお、HANAバージョンアップデートを計画する前に、SRテンプレートを利用してOSアップデートの要否を事前にご確認いただけますようお願いします。列"OS Update Required"の値がYESになっている場合、該当ターゲットHANAバージョンへアップデートする前にOSアップデートが必要であることを示しております。

entry.title: One Quote for Service: In-House Repair and Advanced Execution into the Solution Quotation
entry.content:
The Vision of One Quote for Service

Service organizations running SAP S/4HANA have always had a robust quoting capability through the Service Quotation,  At the same time, as customer engagements grow in complexity combining physical goods, recurring services, service contracts, and subscription offerings within a single deal a second, complementary path has emerged which is Solution Quotation.

The Solution Quotation is designed for the broader commercial picture. Where a Service Quotation excels in service-centric scenarios, the Solution Quotation excels as service quote additionally it goes further as the single document that enable customer to combine sales items (physical goods), sales contract items, service items, service contract items (AMC), and subscription items in one offering. A customer acquiring a machine, its installation service, an annual maintenance contract, and a software subscription can be quoted in one document, accepted in one step, and fulfilled through respective connected document flow. Customers also have option to quote individual item/s with solution quotation. Business sees value in this unified commercial approach now have a genuine choice to adopt the Solution Quotation as the single quoting object for their broader solution and service business.

With the two features delivered in SAP S/4HANA 2205 FPS02 — In-House Repair via Solution Quotation and Service with Advanced Execution in Solution Quotation the Solution Quotation reaches functional parity with the Service Quotation for service-specific scenarios. 

1. In-House Repair via Solution Quotation 

The repair workshop process can now be initiated and governed from within a solution quotation similar to service quotation, connecting the customer-facing commercial offer directly to the physical repair workflow. In-House Repair, Assignment Block has been introduced, you can add Insert or assign existing In-house Service Object

For example here I have inserted Product, Equipment and Serial Number and Save, it created In-House Service Object

navigate to In-house Service Object, and there you can see Button to Create Solution Quotation, This you can use if process started from In-House Service Object and now you need to decide to create solution quotation/service quotation or service order, further you can see process flow start with Solution Quotation, same is also visualized in Solution Quotation's Progress Monitor.  For more details follow the help document 

 

 

 

2. Service with Advanced Execution — Now Starts from a Solution Quotation

Until this release, the Service with Advanced Execution process had one entry point: the Service Quotation. If your customer's deal combined a complex execution scope — say, a major asset overhaul — with physical goods, a subscription, or an annual maintenance contract, you needed more than one quotation document to cover it. That workaround ends here.

SAP S/4HANA 2205 FPS02 brings execution order items (item category MSQ1) into the Solution Quotation (transaction type SRVP). One quotation. Full solution scope. Complex execution included.

Solution Quote → Plan → Accept → Execute → Bill — all connected, all traceable back to one document.

  • Add execution order items to the Solution Quotation if needed for your business alongside sales items, service items, AMC, or subscription items. The commercial scope  price, billing model, validity, is agreed at the quotation level, before any execution planning begins.

  • Trigger planning with a single action. In the Execution Order Items view, select "Send to Planning" on any item in Open or In Process status. The system automatically creates a Maintenance Order and hands the scope to your planning team — no separate transaction, no manual handoff

     

    On save it create Maintenance Order

     

  • Plan in Maintenance Management. Operations, labor, materials, work centers, scheduling — all planned in detail within the linked Maintenance Order. Planned resource data flows back to inform pricing on the quotation.

        

  • Accept the quotation to trigger execution. Once planning is complete, navigate back to the Solution Quotation and record customer acceptance. The system automatically creates the follow-up Service Order, links it to the Maintenance Order, and the execution chain is live.

  • Billing driven by the Service Order — two paths supported:

    • Billing on Completion → Billing Document Request created on service completion.
    • Itemized Billing → Debit Memo Request created for granular, line-item billing as work progresses.

  • Track everything in one place. The Solution Quotation Progress Monitor (Manage Solution Quotations – Version 2, App ID: F7671) now shows Maintenance Orders as process flow nodes — for both the Solution Quotation → Maintenance Order and the Service Order → Maintenance Order flows. Full document chain, one screen.

      

 

SAP S/4HANA 2205 FPS02 marks a deliberate step toward the One Quote vision. By anchoring In-House Repair and Advanced Execution within the Solution Quotation, SAP closes two longstanding commercial gaps.

For customers, this means fewer manual touchpoints, transparent cost commitments, and a single document that governs service from offer to invoice. For organizations already using Solution Quotation for sales, subscriptions, and service contracts, these features make it equally capable for the most operationally complex service scenarios.

entry.title: E-learning Available: Driving Finance Transformation by Converting to SAP S/4HANA
entry.content:
For many organisations running SAP ERP, the journey to SAP S/4HANA represents far more than a technical upgrade - it is a fundamental transformation of the finance function. Legacy ERP finance architectures rely on separate data structures for financial accounting, controlling, and asset accounting, requiring complex reconciliation processes, batch-driven reporting cycles, and significant manual effort during period-end close. These constraints limit real-time financial visibility, slow down decision-making, and create a growing gap between what the business needs and what the finance organization can deliver.

Converting to SAP S/4HANA Finance offers the opportunity to fundamentally re-architect how financial data is captured, processed, and reported - unlocking real-time insights, simplifying the data model, and enabling a faster, more intelligent close. To help finance professionals, project team members, and consultants navigate this transformation, this 1.5-hour e-learning course guides learners through the essential finance changes, conversion activities, and data migration steps involved in moving to SAP S/4HANA Finance.

What You’ll Learn

This e-learning walks through the key finance activities involved in an SAP S/4HANA conversion, from getting your SAP ERP system ready for the move to validating data and completing FI/CO tasks after go-live. Along the way, you'll see practical system checks, real project insights, and guidance to help ensure a smooth and successful conversion.

The e-learning course contains below topics with an assessment at the end to test your knowledge.  

  • Identify and complete key preparation activities in SAP ERP to ensure readiness for an SAP S/4HANA conversion.
  • Perform and validate finance-related conversion tasks in SAP S/4HANA, including verifying data migration to the new data model.
  • Apply FI/CO post-conversion responsibilities and best practices using insights and lessons learned from real project experiences.

entry.title: SAP EarlyWatch Alert: A Unified View of Missing Side-Effect Solving Notes
entry.content:
Introduction

Maintaining the stability and reliability of SAP systems involves more than implementing SAP Notes to resolve known issues. In some cases, an implemented SAP Note may introduce a known side effect that requires a corresponding side-effect solving SAP Note.

Identifying missing side-effect solving SAP Notes is essential for assessing potential risks and determining appropriate corrective actions. The SAP EarlyWatch Alert Service helps customers address this challenge by detecting missing solving notes and triggering alerts for affected systems. However, locating and reviewing this information can be challenging when the findings are spread across multiple system components and different sections of the SAP EarlyWatch Alert Report.

To make this process easier, a new functionality is available in the SAP EarlyWatch Alert experience for on-premise and private cloud systems.

What's New?

Get the complete picture at a glance! A new card in the Support tab of the System Details page in SAP for Me now provides a consolidated list of missing side-effect solving SAP Notes identified by the SAP EarlyWatch Alert Service across your system's components—making it easier to spot potential issues, gain insights, and take action.

No more piecing together information from different sources! Previously, these details were scattered across individual components in the SAP EarlyWatch Alert Solution Finder results and various sections of the SAP EarlyWatch Alert Report.

With this enhancement, users can access the relevant information in one place instead of navigating through multiple components and report sections to build a complete picture.

Where Can You Find the New Overview?

The functionality is available for on-premise and private cloud systems.

To access the overview:

  1. Open the relevant system's System Details page under Systems and Provisioning in SAP for Me.
  2. Navigate to the Support tab.
  3. Locate the new card for missing side-effect solving notes.
  4. Review the consolidated findings across the system's components.

This provides a convenient starting point for understanding which missing notes have been identified and may require attention.

Which Components Are Covered?

The functionality covers the components evaluated by the SAP EarlyWatch Alert Service for missing side-effect solving SAP Notes. The applicable component coverage and exclusions depend on the supported checks and system type.

For a detailed list of the components included in the checks, as well as those excluded from the overview, refer to SAP Note 3362629 – Missing Side Effects Solving SAP Notes Detected by SAP EarlyWatch Alert Service.

 

How Can You Use This Information?

The consolidated overview helps you identify missing side-effect solving SAP Notes and prioritize further investigation.

When reviewing the findings, consider the following steps:

  1. Review the missing notes listed for your system.
  2. Examine the corresponding SAP Notes and their relevance to the affected components.
  3. Assess the potential impact on your system and business processes.
  4. Determine the appropriate corrective actions based on the applicable SAP Note instructions and your system's requirements.

The overview supports your analysis and decision-making. The relevance of each finding should be assessed in the context of your individual system before implementing any changes.

“Spot missing  SAP Notes. Stay ahead of side effects.”!
